plan: In a second-price auction (pay second-highest bid if I win), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds both competitors' bids (guaranteeing non-negative profit) and lose otherwise, avoiding overpaying. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no incentive to shade up or down. With no prior history in this single-round game, I'll bid my true value of $25 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $18, I should bid exactly $18 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value of $31 maximizes my expected profit - I won't overpay since I only pay what the second-highest bidder bid, and I ensure I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids while never paying more than my value.
